Every endpoint maps to ≥ 1 query / mutation on a `data-model.md` entity:

| Endpoint | Maps to |

| `GET /courses` | `SELECT FROM courses WHERE org_id=$1 AND (status='published' OR caller-is-owner-or-admin) ORDER BY id` (cursor: UUID v7) |

| `PATCH /courses/{id}/lessons/reorder` | `BEGIN; UPDATE lessons SET sequence=... WHERE id=... AND course_id=$cid (batch); COMMIT` |

**Check 5 — OpenAPI ↔ sequence:** ✓ with conscious deferral

The lessons-slice retains its endpoint-level sequence match from run 2:

| Sequence branch (endpoint-level publish-lesson) | Spec response |
|---|---|
| `alt lesson not found OR not owned` → `404` | `responses.NotFound` (`lesson.not_found`) |
| `alt lesson not found OR not owned` → `403` | `responses.Forbidden` (`lesson.forbidden`) |
| Happy path `200` | `responses.200` |
| Outbox INSERT in same transaction → retry-safe | `Idempotency-Key` header marked required |

For the **9 newly added endpoints**, only **container-level** sequences
exist (sad.md §6 US-01..US-10). Endpoint-level sequences with
HTTP-status-coded alt-branches are **deferred** — the team chose not to
run `complete-sequence-diagrams` in this pass (would have produced 9
additional sequences this iteration). Consequences for this report:

- Error responses whose code is named in a container-level alt-branch
  message ⇒ `confidence: high` in the field-origin table (because the
  message text directly names the code).
- Error responses whose code is only inferred from PRD AC text (no
  explicit alt-branch in any sequence) ⇒ `confidence: medium`.
- Happy-path response shapes are `high` whenever they map 1:1 to a
  data-model.md table; otherwise `medium` (notably `PeerCompletionSignal`
  which is aggregated).

This is a conscious deviation, not a drift finding. The next iteration
of the team can run `sdlc-complete-sequences course-lesson-mvp` to lift
the `medium` fields to `high`.

## Polymorphic exception (carried forward from run 2)

`LessonBlock.payload` and `AddBlockRequest.payload` use
`additionalProperties: true`. The api-forge default forbids this on
response shapes (leakage risk).

The exception is deliberate: per ADR-0001, payload is **polymorphic per
`block_type`** with four distinct shapes:

| `block_type` | Payload shape |
|---|---|
| `text` | `{content: string}` |
| `video_embed` | `{url: string, provider: string}` |
| `image` | `{url: string, alt: string}` |
| `code` | `{language: string, content: string}` |

Tightening this into four discriminated variants requires JSON Schema
2020-12 conditional schemas (`if/then/else` per `block_type`) — supported
by OpenAPI 3.1 but produces a noisy spec. Deferred to a follow-up run.

## Deprecation note — `POST /lessons`

The legacy top-level `POST /lessons` (v1.0.0) is preserved in the v1.1.0
contract with `deprecated: true`. Reasoning:

- PRD US-02 reads as "create a lesson **inside** a course" — a nested
  path (`POST /courses/{id}/lessons`) reflects the parent-child
  relationship more honestly than passing `course_id` in the body.
- Existing FE / handler consumers of v1.0.0 continue to work without
  client-side changes; new consumers should use the canonical nested
  route.

**Migration path recommendation:**

1. v1.1 (this run): both routes work; new code uses `POST /courses/{id}/lessons`.
2. v1.2 (next minor): FE migrated; any v1.0-style call logged with a
   deprecation warning header (`Sunset: <date>`, RFC 8594).
3. v2.0 (next major): legacy route removed; bump to `info.version: 2.0.0`.

No removal in this PR — only the `deprecated: true` flag.
